newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma calls for 20 pct cut in gas use.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma calls for 20 pct cut in gas use.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma has ordered the government and local administrations to reduce gas consumption by 20 per cent from current levels, the presidential press office said on Wednesday.
The office also said that Kuchma had ordered the government to work out a two-year programme for a "gradual reduction in gas consumption."

But it was unclear whether Kuchma was aiming to cut demand by increase efficiency in gas use in Ukraine, or taking a swipe at the dozen or so trading enterprises which now import natural gas by reducing the volumes they could import by a fifth.

"Twenty per cent is a realistic goal -- if gas is consumed rationally. But it still unclear whether the president meant domestic consumption or the need for a reduction in imports," a source at the State Oil and Gas Committee said.
"If the last one is true, then this could be seen as a serious intention to strike the gas traders. Of course, they want to import more and to earn more," the source, who declined to be named, added.
The Ukrainian government introduced a scheme in 1995 which allowed a dozen or so private and state-owned companies to import gas from Russia and Central Asia.

Prime Minister Lazarenko, the initiator and defender of the gas distribution scheme, maintains that the scheme is a success, because it shifted debts owed by Ukraine to gas suppliers like Russia and Turkmenistan to the companies.
But Kuchma said that the scheme has failed to solve a non-payments crisis between gas suppliers and consumers within Ukraine.

"The non-existence of real market mechanisms and monopolisation of the energy market has not led to the solution of debt problems, and has transferred it from foreign (debts) to the domestic ones," Kuchma said in a order.
Some of the gas importers, including state-owned entities, have been accused of not paying taxes to the state and salaries to workers.
The parliamentary commission in charge of energy said recently that the gas import scheme was partly to blame for over $2 billion arrears in Ukraine for unpaid salaries.
Kuchma said that Ukraine's total domestic gas debts totalled 4.5 billion hryvnias ($2.5 billion).

Ukraine is expected to import up to 53 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas from Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and up to 20 bcm of gas from the Central Asian states of Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan in 1997. Domestic output stands at about 18 bcm.
Official statistics show that in the first quarter of 1997 alone Ukraine imported gas worth $1.8 billion, accounting for 44 per cent of the former Soviet republic's total imports.
Oil and gas analysts estimate Ukraine's gas debt to Russia for 1991-1994 supplies at $3.5 billion as well as up to $700 million owed to Turkmenistan over the same period.
Kiev is still in a row with the Turkmen leadership over about $300 million in gas debts accumulated in 1996 and the first four months of 1997 by a private firm recently forced out of the market.

Kuchma also put off a trip to the Turkmen capital of Ashgabat recently, after Turkeminstan said Ukraine's government should take responsibility for the gas debt while Kiev insisted that is was not the guarantor for private firms' debts.
Over 60 percent of Ukraine's gas imports are consumed by state enterprises and the remainder by private companies.
